We are a team of 8th graders coming from a secondary school called Trưng Vương. We are a creative, curious and passionate group about technology, exploration and development. We love taking ideas and bringing them to life through design and codes.

We focus on team building and value each other's ideas. We also try to discover new things and make sure every member gets to contribute and sharpen their skills.
summary: "A Space's Corner" is a research-oriented platform designed to connect Earth science and interplanetary exploration. We offer an organized collection of theoretic locations using geographical characteristics and environmental temperature, subsequently comparing them with extraterrestrial landscapes.By identifying terrestrial environments that resembles unorthodox conditions, we aim to provide valuable insights to aid subsequent Moon and Mars objectives. Our website also covers Earth geology, extreme conditions and astrobiology in order to support researchers, students and space enthusiasts in investigating potential analog sites. Our ambitions reach much further, though. Our team focuses on envisioning a brighter tomorrow for humanity and scientific breakthroughs beyond the cosmos. Earth may be the starting point, but it certainly isn't the ending.

Math Matrix's Project Solution:
A Space’s Corner is an educational website designed to help users identify and explore Earth locations that serve as analogs for permanent Moon base sites and Mars. For each location, we guide users through everything from its geography and physical structure to its exploration history, scientific importance, and notable discoveries.
How Does Our Solution Work:
Users navigate an interactive map of Earth’s planetary analog sites, pairing real terrestrial locations with their corresponding regions on the Moon and Mars. Selecting a site unlocks structured, easy-to-digest breakdowns covering its geography, key geological features, role in space research, and major scientific findings—turning complex planetary science into an accessible, hands-on experience.

Benefits & Intended Impact:
A Space’s Corner benefits students, researchers, and space enthusiasts by:

  • Educating users on planetary analogs and how Earth’s extreme environments mirror conditions on the Moon and Mars.
  • Demonstrating practical, science-backed comparisons across geography, terrain, and average surface temperatures to show how scientists test habitats and exploration technologies.
  • Bridging the gap between open space agency datasets and accessible learning through interactive 2D/3D maps, a built-in dictionary, and structured location breakdowns.

Our Goal:

To make open data from NASA and international space agencies more accessible, helping learners and aspiring researchers explore how terrestrial geology prepares humanity for future Moon bases and Mars missions. While we aimed to cover key analog regions across the globe, our current database focuses on primary study sites and does not yet include every emerging planetary analog location worldwide—something we plan to expand in future updates.
